title: 1. Organisation Structure & Reporting Lines
body:
**DR. NISHITA'S CLINIC – ORGANISATION STRUCTURE**

*Management → Core Departments → Lean Support Functions*

| **Dr. Nishita Ranka CEO & Medical Director Clinical Vision • Medical Governance • Patient Safety • Treatment Standards • Strategic Direction** |

↓

| **Shreyas Bagmar COO Business Operations • Financial Governance • Growth • Systems • Organisational Performance** |

↓

| **Naga Chief of Staff (COS) Execution • Department Coordination • KPIs & Governance • People & Systems • Cross-department Accountability** |

**↓ CORE OPERATING STRUCTURE**

| **Front Office & Patient Experience** | **Procedure Operations (Therapy Department)** | **Procedure Floor & Stock Control** | **Pharmacy & Lab** | **Administration & Support Functions** |

| **• Front Office Lead**  • Reception, Billing & Records Coordinator  • Patient Counsellor & Treatment Conversion Coordinator  • Consultation Scheduling & Recall Coordinator  • Procedure Scheduling & Recall Coordinator  • Clinical Photography & Documentation Coordinator  • Patient Flow & Doctor Coordination Executive | **• Lead Therapist (L5)**  • Senior Therapist (L4)  • Therapist (L3)  • Junior Therapist (L2)  • Trainee Therapist (L1) | **• Procedure Floor & Stock Control Coordinator** | **• Pharmacy Manager**  • Pharmacist  • Lab Operations / Lab Technician | **• Accounts & Finance — Accounts Executive / Accountant**  **• HR & Administration — HR & Admin Executive**  **• MIS / Systems & Data — MIS Coordinator**  **• Housekeeping & Facility Support — Housekeeping Supervisor / Coordinator** |

| DOCTORS / CLINICAL TEAM — Direct Clinical Governance by Dr. Nishita • Dr. Nishita Ranka • Associate Doctors • Junior Doctors | EXTERNAL MARKETING AGENCY — Coordinated by Management / COS • Digital marketing & campaigns • Content / creative support • Performance reporting & lead-generation coordination |

**ADMINISTRATION PRINCIPLE**

Administration is a lean support umbrella. Accounts, HR, MIS/Systems and Housekeeping are each handled by their designated department owner; additional layers or multiple positions should be added only when workload requires them. Marketing remains outsourced to the external agency.

**REPORTING PRINCIPLES**

* All operational department owners report to the Chief of Staff (COS).
* Dr. Nishita retains direct clinical authority over Doctors, clinical protocols and patient-safety decisions.
* Pharmacy includes Lab operations.
* Administration supports all departments through Accounts, HR/Admin, MIS/Systems and Housekeeping/Facilities.
* External Marketing Agency is coordinated by Management/COS and is not shown as an internal staffing hierarchy.
* Every department should have clear ownership, defined handoffs and no unowned pending work.

title: 0. About the Front Office Manual (v1.1)
body:
**DR. NISHITA'S CLINIC**

FRONT OFFICE & PATIENT EXPERIENCE
OPERATING STRUCTURE

Individual Role Charters • KPIs • Handoff Rules • Daily Checklists • Control Board

| **ONE PATIENT JOURNEY • CLEAR OWNERSHIP • ZERO UNOWNED HANDOFFS** |

**Purpose:** Formalise the front office around the actual patient journey, with defined ownership from enquiry and arrival through consultation, counselling, procedure readiness, recall and visit closure.

Version 1.1 • Governance Integrated • Internal Management Document • September 2026

title: 1. Department Structure
body:
| **ROLE** | **PRIMARY OWNERSHIP** | **CORE SYSTEM / REGISTER** |
| 1. Reception, Billing & Records Coordinator | Arrival, greeting, registration, records, payment clearance, billing and same-day recommendation capture. | Patient/packet sheet; billing; Suggested Treatment capture |
| 2. Patient Counsellor & Treatment Conversion Coordinator | Post-consult counselling, pricing, treatment decision and follow-up of unbooked recommendations. | Suggested Treatment pipeline |
| 3. Consultation Scheduling & Recall Coordinator | Enquiry-to-consult booking, confirmations, no-shows and future consultation reviews. | Consultation appointment book; consultation recall list |
| 4. Procedure Scheduling & Recall Coordinator | Procedure booking, completion tracking, next sessions and procedure recalls. | Procedure appointment book; Procedures Done; recall list |
| 5. Clinical Photography & Documentation Coordinator | Take clinical photographs, correct upload/tagging and visual-record completeness. | Photography/documentation queue |
| 6. Patient Flow & Doctor Coordination Executive | Physical flow, readiness, Associate/Junior Doctor → Dr. Nishita coordination and wait-time communication. | Live patient-flow board |
| Lead: Front Office & Patient Experience Lead | Department-wide ownership, handoffs, exceptions, pending queues and daily closure. | Front Office Control Board |

title: 2. Master Patient Flow
body:
| **APPOINTMENT → ARRIVAL → REGISTRATION/RECORDS → PAYMENT → HISTORY/DOCUMENTS → PHOTOGRAPHY → ASSOCIATE/JUNIOR DOCTOR → DR. NISHITA → COUNSELLING → PROCEDURE / LAB / PHARMACY → NEXT APPOINTMENT → EXIT** |

Front Office owns the administrative and patient-experience journey. Associate/Junior Doctors and Dr. Nishita own clinical assessment and medical decisions. Once a procedure patient is clinically ready, documented and financially cleared, Front Office hands the patient to Procedure Operations and receives the patient back for recall/next appointment and visit closure.

title: 3. Non-Negotiable Department Rules
body:
* No consultation or procedure begins without required financial clearance, except a documented authorised exception.
* No patient is sent to Dr. Nishita until the pre-consultation readiness requirements and Associate/Junior Doctor stage are complete, except a doctor-directed exception.
* No front-office employee independently diagnoses, recommends, changes treatment, or changes a clinically prescribed interval.
* Every treatment recommended must be captured and assigned a commercial status/owner.
* Every next review or multi-session treatment must leave as Booked, Recall Created, Course Completed, or a documented exception.
* No patient handoff is complete until the receiving function accepts ownership.
* No patient leaves with an unexplained pending action.
* WhatsApp communication does not replace the appointment book, patient record, billing record, Suggested Treatment pipeline, Procedures Done record or recall list.

title: 4. Reception, Billing & Records Coordinator
body:
**Purpose:** Own the administrative opening and financial clearance of every visit, ensure the correct patient record is ready, and ensure same-day treatment recommendations are captured for downstream follow-up.

## Core responsibilities

* Stand, greet with smile and acknowledge every arriving patient promptly and professionally.
* Identify whether patient is new, existing, consultation-only, procedure-only, or consultation + procedure.
* For new patients: ensure New Patient Form/registration is completed and attached to the correct record.
* For existing patients: retrieve previous treatment forms, relevant prior records, prescriptions/reports and make them accessible to the clinical team.
* Collect consultation/procedure payment before service as applicable; generate invoice/receipt and mark Financially Cleared.
* Verify package/session balance for prepaid/package patients rather than charging incorrectly.
* After consultation, ensure every recommended treatment is entered into the Suggested Treatment pipeline on the same day.
* Ensure any doctor-written next review instruction is visible to the appropriate scheduler before visit closure.

## Role boundaries — should not

* Independently decide discounts, refunds, complimentary services or payment deferrals outside authority.
* Certify/reconcile her own daily collections without independent verification.
* Interpret blood reports or give medical advice.
* Alter a doctor's treatment recommendation.

## Daily checklist

* Opening: confirm billing system, appointment list, cash float if applicable, payment devices and patient forms are ready.
* For each arrival: complete new/existing-patient readiness steps and financial clearance.
* After each consultation: capture recommended treatment and route to counsellor/scheduler.
* End of day: verify no completed consultation/procedure is missing billing/payment status; submit collections for independent reconciliation; verify no recommendation is uncaptured.

## KPIs

| **KPI** | **STANDARD / MEASURE** |
| Greeting/check-in compliance | Target: ≥95% observed compliance; move toward 100% |
| Payment-before-service compliance | 100% except documented authorised exceptions |
| Billing accuracy | ≥99%; track corrections/cancellations separately |
| Suggested Treatment capture | 100% of documented recommendations captured same day |
| Record readiness | ≥98% of existing patient records/treatment forms ready before clinical handoff |
| Daily reconciliation variance | ₹0 unexplained variance |

## Handoff rule

Hands patient to Photography/Documentation or Patient Flow only after registration/records and required financial clearance are complete. After consultation, hands the recommendation record to the Counsellor and next-review instruction to the appropriate Scheduler.

## Escalate when

Payment dispute; unexplained billing mismatch; missing historic record materially affecting visit; patient refuses required payment; unauthorised discount/refund request; suspected manipulation of billing or records.

title: 5. Patient Counsellor & Treatment Conversion Coordinator
body:
**Purpose:** Own the non-medical counselling and commercial follow-through of every doctor-recommended treatment until it reaches a defined outcome.

## Core responsibilities

* Receive the doctor's documented treatment recommendation after consultation.
* Explain the treatment journey, number of sessions/interval as prescribed, logistics, pricing and approved package/payment options.
* Show approved educational material and before/after material where appropriate.
* Route medical/clinical questions back to the doctor rather than improvising answers.
* Update every Suggested Treatment record to: Counselled, Booked, Considering, Follow-up, Deferred, Declined, Not Suitable or Lost.
* Follow up patients who have been advised treatment but have not booked, using an agreed cadence and respecting patient preferences.
* Capture a meaningful lost/pending reason so management can understand conversion leakage.

## Role boundaries — should not

* Diagnose, independently recommend treatment, promise results, change session count/interval, or provide clinical advice.
* Give unapproved discounts or alter package terms.
* Own routine consultation appointment scheduling once treatment counselling is complete.

## Daily checklist

* Review all new recommendations from the day and ensure none remain unassigned.
* Counsel patients after consultation and record outcome immediately.
* Work today's due follow-up queue; document every contact attempt/outcome.
* Hand all patients who agree to proceed to Procedure Scheduling immediately.
* End of day: review all new recommendations for missing status, missing value or missing next action.

## KPIs

| **KPI** | **STANDARD / MEASURE** |
| Same-day recommendation counselling | ≥95% of eligible patients before exit |
| Suggested → Booked conversion | Track by treatment and counsellor; baseline first 30 days then target |
| 7-day / 30-day conversion | Track trend by treatment category |
| Follow-ups due vs completed | ≥95% |
| Unowned/blank Suggested records | 0 |
| Lost reason completeness | ≥95% |
| Suggested value vs booked value | Weekly/monthly management KPI |

## Handoff rule

Receives recommendation from Reception/Treatment Capture after doctor consultation. When patient agrees, hands to Procedure Scheduler with exact documented treatment and any clinically stated timing. If patient does not agree immediately, Counsellor retains ownership until a defined disposition.

## Escalate when

Clinical question; patient dissatisfaction; request for exceptional pricing; conflicting recommendation/documentation; high-value treatment dispute; patient alleges misleading communication.

title: 6. Consultation Scheduling & Recall Coordinator
body:
**Purpose:** Own the consultation calendar from first enquiry through attendance, and ensure every doctor-advised future consultation/review is booked or placed into a recall queue.

## Core responsibilities

* Respond to new consultation enquiries across assigned channels.
* Explain consultation fee before arrival and offer appropriate available slots.
* Book, confirm, reschedule and recover no-show consultations.
* Maintain consultation waitlist and fill released slots.
* At exit, convert doctor-written review instructions into a booked appointment or Recall Due date.
* Run consultation recall queues and document contact/outcome.

## Role boundaries — should not

* Counsel on treatment selection or independently answer medical suitability questions.
* Schedule a procedure based on assumption rather than a documented treatment plan.
* Leave 'review after X weeks/months' only in the patient file without operational booking/recall.

## Daily checklist

* Start day: review today's consultations, confirmations, waitlist and unconfirmed patients.
* During day: work new enquiries within response-time standard.
* Recover cancellations/no-shows and refill capacity where possible.
* Before close: ensure today's doctor-advised review dates have either appointments or recalls.
* Prepare next-day consultation confirmation queue.

## KPIs

| **KPI** | **STANDARD / MEASURE** |
| Enquiry response time | Define channel SLA; monitor median and >SLA cases |
| Enquiry → consultation booking % | Track weekly |
| Consultation confirmation rate | ≥95% |
| Consultation show rate | Track and improve |
| Missed-call / uncontacted lead recovery | ≥95% worked same day |
| Doctor-advised review capture | 100% booked or recalled |
| Unowned consultation recalls | 0 |

## Handoff rule

Hands booked patient to Reception on arrival. Receives future review instruction from Reception/visit-closure process and owns it until booked, declined or appropriately closed.

## Escalate when

Repeated inability to contact high-priority patient; overbooking/capacity conflict; VIP/sensitive scheduling issue; repeated no-show; patient complaint about appointment handling.

title: 7. Procedure Scheduling & Recall Coordinator
body:
**Purpose:** Convert agreed treatment plans into actual procedure appointments, maintain procedure completion records and ensure multi-session treatment continuity.

## Core responsibilities

* Receive confirmed treatment plan from Counsellor/doctor record.
* Schedule procedure according to documented clinical timing and available procedure capacity.
* Confirm procedure appointments and required pre-visit instructions approved by the clinical team.
* Maintain Procedures Done record after confirmation of actual completion.
* For every completed multi-session procedure, create the next appointment or recall based on the documented plan.
* Track patients due for next sessions and work the recall queue.
* Prepare the upcoming procedure schedule for Procedure Operations.

## Role boundaries — should not

* Decide treatment interval, provider, clinical suitability or procedure sequence independently.
* Mark a procedure Done based only on booking; completion must be confirmed.
* Own room allocation or run procedure-room operations.

## Daily checklist

* Review today's procedures, confirmations, cancellations and likely gaps.
* Schedule newly converted patients.
* Update Procedures Done only after completion confirmation.
* Ensure each completed course has Next Session Booked / Recall Created / Course Completed.
* Prepare next-day and 7-day procedure schedule for operational planning.

## KPIs

| **KPI** | **STANDARD / MEASURE** |
| Agreed treatment → procedure booked | Track same-day and 7-day booking |
| Procedure confirmation rate | ≥95% |
| Procedure no-show/cancellation rate | Track by reason |
| Procedures Done completeness | 100% of completed procedures recorded |
| Next session booked or recall created | 100% for multi-session plans |
| Overdue procedure recalls | 0 unexplained overdue |
| Procedure calendar utilisation | Track by day/time/category |

## Handoff rule

Receives treatment decision from Counsellor. On procedure day, Reception confirms financial clearance; Procedure Scheduler hands the scheduled case to Procedure Operations. After clinical completion, receives confirmation back to update Done/next-session status.

## Escalate when

Clinical interval unclear; requested slot conflicts with doctor/room/resource availability; repeated cancellation; package/session discrepancy; procedure completed but documentation/payment status inconsistent.

title: 8. Clinical Photography & Documentation Coordinator
body:
**Purpose:** Maintain a complete, consistent and retrievable visual clinical record for all patients and visits where photography is required.

## Core responsibilities

* Confirm correct patient identity before photography.
* Follow treatment/indication-specific photography protocol and required views.
* Maintain consistency of angles, framing, background and lighting as far as operationally possible.
* Upload photographs to the correct patient record promptly with correct date/visit tagging.
* Retrieve previous photographs for comparison when required.
* Flag missing, incorrect, poor-quality or mis-tagged images for correction.
* Ensure photographs are handled only through approved clinic devices/storage/workflows.

## Role boundaries — should not

* Use patient images for marketing without the required consent/workflow.
* Keep clinical photographs casually on personal phones.
* Decide whether a clinical photograph can be omitted when protocol/doctor requires it.

## Daily checklist

* Review today's appointment list for patients requiring photography.
* Complete and upload images before clinical handoff where required.
* Ensure prior images are retrievable for returning patients.
* End-of-day check: all eligible patients have complete, correctly uploaded records or documented exception.

## KPIs

| **KPI** | **STANDARD / MEASURE** |
| Required photography completion | Target near 100% |
| Same-visit upload completeness | ≥98%, progressing to 100% |
| Incorrect patient/tagging events | 0 |
| Retakes due to quality/protocol failure | Track and reduce |
| Missing prior-photo retrieval issues | Track and reduce |

## Handoff rule

Receives patient after registration/records as appropriate. Once photography/documentation is complete, updates readiness and hands to Patient Flow / Associate Doctor stage.

## Escalate when

Consent uncertainty; incorrect patient/image association; missing critical historic images; device/storage failure; suspected data/privacy issue.

title: 9. Patient Flow & Doctor Coordination Executive
body:
**Purpose:** Own the patient's physical journey through the consultation floor, ensure readiness before each clinical handoff, minimise avoidable waiting and keep Dr. Nishita's consultation flow organised.

## Core responsibilities

* Maintain live status of every patient physically present in clinic.
* Confirm pre-consultation readiness before routing to Associate/Junior Doctor.
* After Associate/Junior Doctor stage, ensure patient is Ready for Dr. Nishita.
* Coordinate the queue into Dr. Nishita's room and prevent avoidable gaps.
* Have relevant previous/current photographs and records ready for display/retrieval.
* Inside/around Dr. Nishita's room, assist with records/before-afters and capture/route operational instructions without giving independent medical advice.
* Proactively communicate delays and expected waiting to patients.
* After Dr. Nishita consultation, route patient to Counsellor, Procedure pathway, Lab, Pharmacy or exit workflow as appropriate.

## Role boundaries — should not

* Override clinical priority set by doctors.
* Interpret clinical information or independently advise patients.
* Send an unprepared patient to Dr. Nishita simply to reduce visible waiting time.

## Daily checklist

* Opening: review doctor schedules, expected consultation load and known sensitive/priority cases.
* Maintain live statuses: Arrived / Preparation / With Associate / Ready for Nishita / With Nishita / Counselling / Procedure-Lab-Pharmacy / Exit.
* Monitor waiting time continuously and intervene/communicate before dissatisfaction builds.
* Ensure the next appropriate patient is ready when Dr. Nishita becomes available.
* End of day: no patient remains physically or digitally in an unexplained in-clinic status.

## KPIs

| **KPI** | **STANDARD / MEASURE** |
| Ready-for-Doctor completeness | ≥98% with required prerequisites |
| Avoidable idle gaps between consults | Track and reduce |
| Wait-time communication compliance | 100% beyond agreed threshold |
| Patients waiting beyond escalation threshold | Track by cause |
| Incorrect/premature handoffs | 0 |
| Unexplained live-board statuses at close | 0 |

## Handoff rule

Receives administratively prepared/photographed patient, routes through Associate/Junior Doctor and then Dr. Nishita. After consultation, explicitly hands to Counsellor or other next function. For procedure patients, Front Office ultimately hands over only when Ready for Procedure.

## Escalate when

Clinical priority conflict; prolonged doctor delay; angry/waiting patient; missing prerequisite that cannot be resolved promptly; queue overload; patient safety concern.

title: 10. Front Office & Patient Experience Lead
body:
**Purpose:** Own the performance of the entire front-office patient journey, not individual clerical tasks. Ensure every queue has an owner, every handoff is accepted and every day closes with no unexplained pending work.

## Core responsibilities

* Run the front-office opening huddle and allocate backups/coverage.
* Monitor one Front Office Control Board rather than chasing six separate people.
* Ensure handoff rules are followed and intervene when work is stuck between functions.
* Review patient wait times, uncontacted enquiries, unbooked recommendations, recalls, missing photos, payment exceptions and complaints.
* Conduct end-of-day Zero Unowned Pending check.
* Coach team members against their KPIs and escalate repeated control failures to Naga/Clinic Manager.
* Maintain cross-training so absence of one person does not collapse the function.

## Role boundaries — should not

* Become the person who personally completes every missed task.
* Approve financial/HR/clinical exceptions outside delegated authority.
* Allow staff to bypass ownership because 'someone else will do it'.

## Daily checklist

* Opening huddle: staffing, doctor schedule, consultation/procedure load, VIP/sensitive cases, absences, known bottlenecks.
* Midday control check: queues, waiting, uncontacted leads, pending recommendations, photography gaps, payment exceptions.
* End-of-day closure: verify every visit and queue has a status/owner/next action.
* Send concise exception summary to Naga/Clinic Manager.

## KPIs

| **KPI** | **STANDARD / MEASURE** |
| Unowned pending items at close | 0 |
| Front-office SOP compliance | ≥95%, moving toward 100% |
| Patient waiting exceptions | Downward trend |
| Uncontacted enquiries at close | 0 or documented exception |
| Missing recommendation/recall/photo/payment records | 0 unexplained |
| Founder/Naga interventions caused by routine front-office failure | Downward trend |
| Cross-coverage readiness | At least one trained backup per critical function |

## Handoff rule

Receives exceptions from all six roles. Resolves within delegated authority or escalates to Naga/Clinic Manager. Does not routinely escalate Green issues to founders.

## Escalate when

Repeated SOP breach; material financial exception; serious patient complaint; staffing failure threatening operations; data/privacy issue; suspected misconduct; unresolved Amber issue.

title: 11. Formal Handoff Rules
body:
| **FROM** | **TO** | **HANDOFF IS COMPLETE ONLY WHEN** |
| Consultation Scheduler | Reception | Appointment exists; patient arrives and is acknowledged/check-in starts. |
| Reception / Records | Photography / Flow | Registration/record retrieval and required financial clearance completed; missing items explicitly flagged. |
| Photography | Associate / Patient Flow | Required images uploaded/tagged; prior images accessible where relevant. |
| Associate/Junior Doctor | Patient Flow / Dr. Nishita | History/preliminary clinical work-up documented; relevant reports/records available; patient marked Ready for Dr. Nishita. |
| Dr. Nishita / Consultation | Reception Treatment Capture + Counsellor | Recommendation, prescription/investigations and review instruction are documented sufficiently for downstream action. |
| Treatment Capture | Counsellor | Suggested Treatment entry exists and is assigned. |
| Counsellor | Procedure Scheduler | Patient has agreed to proceed; exact documented treatment/plan and relevant timing are visible. |
| Procedure Scheduler + Reception | Procedure Operations | Procedure booked/confirmed; patient arrived; required consultation/documentation completed; payment/package financially cleared; case marked Ready for Procedure. |
| Procedure Operations | Procedure Scheduler / Front Office | Actual procedure completion confirmed; session/course status and doctor-directed next interval available. |
| Front Office | Pharmacy / Lab | Prescription/test advice documented; patient directed; status recorded. |
| Front Office | Exit | Today's visit closed; all next actions booked, recalled, completed, declined or explicitly owned. |

title: 12. New vs Existing Patient Readiness Checklist
body:
| **READINESS ITEM** | **NEW** | **EXISTING** |
| Patient identity/check-in completed | Required | Required |
| Consultation payment cleared | Required | Required |
| New Patient Form | Required | Not applicable |
| Existing patient record retrieved | Not applicable | Required |
| Previous treatment forms | If relevant/provided | Required if prior treatment |
| Previous photographs | If available | Required if relevant |
| Previous prescriptions/history | If provided | Retrieve if relevant |
| Updated history / new reports | Required as applicable | Required as applicable |
| Current photography | As protocol requires | As protocol requires |
| Associate/Junior Doctor consultation | Required per clinic workflow | Required per clinic workflow |
| Ready for Dr. Nishita status | Only after prerequisites | Only after prerequisites |

title: 13. Visit Closure Rules
body:
| **NO PATIENT LEAVES WITHOUT THE CURRENT VISIT BEING CLOSED AND THE NEXT REQUIRED ACTION BEING OWNED.** |

* Treatment recommendation: Captured and assigned to Counsellor, or documented as not applicable.
* Payment: Cleared, package/prepaid verified, or authorised exception documented.
* Investigation: Clinic test booked/done, external test pending with recall, declined, or not applicable.
* Pharmacy: Prescription/product direction completed or patient declined/chooses external purchase.
* Next consultation: Booked, Recall Created, no follow-up required, or patient declined.
* Next procedure/session: Booked, Recall Created, Course Completed, or not applicable.
* Photography/documentation: Complete or documented exception.
* Patient physically exits only after required operational handoffs are closed.

title: 15. End-of-Day Zero Unowned Pending Checklist
body:
* Every consultation recommendation entered into Suggested Treatment.
* Every completed procedure entered into Procedures Done.
* Every doctor-advised next review booked or entered into Recall.
* Every multi-session procedure has Next Session Booked / Recall Created / Course Completed.
* Every recommended investigation has a defined status and owner.
* Every required photograph is uploaded or exception documented.
* Every consultation/procedure has financial-clearance status.
* Every pending treatment recommendation has a counsellor and next action.
* Every patient message/enquiry is answered, assigned or documented for next-day follow-up.
* No patient remains on the live floor board without a valid status.

title: 16. Cross-Training & Backup Rules
body:
Specialisation should create accountability, not fragility. Each critical seat must have at least one trained backup.

| **PRIMARY ROLE** | **MINIMUM BACKUP CAPABILITY REQUIRED** |
| Reception/Billing/Records | Second authorised person can check-in, bill, collect payment and retrieve records. |
| Counsellor | Backup can explain approved commercial information and document follow-up; no clinical improvisation. |
| Consultation Scheduler | Backup can book/confirm/reschedule and work recall list. |
| Procedure Scheduler | Backup can book from documented plan and update recall; cannot decide clinical timing. |
| Photography | Backup trained in clinic photography protocol and correct upload/tagging. |
| Patient Flow | Backup can run live board, readiness checks and waiting communication. |
| Front Office Lead | Clinic Manager/Naga can assume control-board and exception role. |

title: 17. Weekly Front Office Review
body:
* Consultation enquiry → booking → arrival funnel.
* Treatment Suggested → Counselled → Booked → Pending/Lost funnel.
* Procedure booked → arrived → done → next session funnel.
* No-show/cancellation reasons.
* Wait-time exceptions and causes.
* Billing/payment exceptions.
* Missing records/photography/documentation.
* Consultation and procedure recall ageing.
* Patient complaints and service-recovery cases.
* Role KPI performance and repeated SOP failures.
* Cross-training gaps and staffing risks.

title: 18. First 14-Day Implementation Plan
body:
| **DAY / PERIOD** | **ACTION** |
| Day 1 | Approve the seven role charters and name the current employee assigned to each seat. |
| Day 2 | Map every existing sheet/register to one owner: Patient/Packet, Suggested Treatment, Consultation Appointments, Procedure Appointments, Procedures Done, Photography, Recalls. |
| Day 3 | Introduce live patient statuses and the Ready for Dr. Nishita gate. |
| Day 4 | Introduce formal handoff rules and payment-before-service verification. |
| Day 5 | Start End-of-Day Zero Unowned Pending checklist. |
| Week 2 | Start role-specific KPI capture; do not judge targets yet — establish baseline. |
| Week 2 | Nominate Front Office Lead and backups for each critical seat. |
| End of Day 14 | Naga + Front Office Lead review bottlenecks, duplicate work, missed handoffs and revise SOPs before locking v1.1. |

title: 20. Governance & Control Framework — Overview
body:
| **ROLE CHARTER → SOP → KPI → CONTROL → EVIDENCE → AUDIT → ESCALATION → CORRECTIVE ACTION** |

The role charters define who performs the work. This governance layer defines who checks it, what evidence proves completion, how exceptions are escalated, and how management ensures the same failure does not recur.

title: 20.1 Governance Hierarchy
body:
| **LEVEL** | **OWNER** | **GOVERNANCE RESPONSIBILITY** |
| L1 — Execution | Six Front Office role owners | Perform the task, record it in the approved system/register, and raise exceptions immediately. |
| L2 — Daily Supervision | Front Office & Patient Experience Lead | Check completeness, manage handoffs/queues, certify daily closure and resolve Green exceptions. |
| L3 — Governance & Control | Naga / Clinic Manager | Review Amber exceptions, KPIs, audit samples, recurring failures, staffing/competency and corrective actions. |
| L4 — Executive Governance | Shreyas | Material financial, commercial, people, policy and operational exceptions; system design and accountability. |
| Clinical Governance | Dr. Nishita | Clinical protocols, medical decisions, patient safety, clinical complaints and clinical exceptions. |

title: 20.2 Governance Cadence
body:
| **CADENCE** | **RUN BY** | **ATTENDEES** | **MANDATORY OUTPUT** |
| Daily opening huddle — 10–15 min | Front Office Lead | Front Office team; clinical liaison as needed | Capacity, staffing, doctor schedule, sensitive patients, known bottlenecks, role coverage. |
| End-of-day closure — 10 min | Front Office Lead | Relevant role owners | Zero Unowned Pending certification; every exception has Owner + Deadline + Status. |
| Weekly governance review — 30–45 min | Naga / Clinic Manager | Front Office Lead; role owners by exception | KPI trends, funnel leakage, recalls, wait times, billing/documentation exceptions, complaints, action tracker. |
| Monthly management review — 60 min | Naga | Shreyas; Dr. Nishita for clinical items; Front Office Lead as required | Material trends, control failures, audit findings, staffing/competency gaps, policy/SOP changes and CAPA closure. |

title: 20.3 Maker–Checker Control Matrix
body:
No material control should rely solely on the person who performed the transaction. The checker verifies evidence, not verbal assurance.

| **CONTROL** | **MAKER / OWNER** | **CHECKER** | **ESCALATION** |
| Consultation/procedure payment & invoice | Reception/Billing Coordinator | Independent Finance/authorised reconciler | Naga → Shreyas if material |
| New patient form / registration | Reception/Billing & Records | Front Office Lead | Naga |
| Previous record/treatment forms ready | Reception/Billing & Records | Patient Flow Coordinator | Front Office Lead → Naga if recurring |
| Required photography complete | Photography Coordinator | Patient Flow Coordinator / FO Lead sample | Front Office Lead → Naga |
| Associate/Junior Doctor stage complete | Associate/Junior Doctor | Clinical workflow / doctor | Dr. Nishita |
| Suggested Treatment captured | Reception/Treatment Capture | Counsellor + FO Lead control check | Naga |
| Suggested Treatment disposition | Counsellor | Front Office Lead | Naga |
| Consultation review booked/recall | Consultation Scheduler | Front Office Lead | Naga |
| Procedure booking / recall | Procedure Scheduler | Front Office Lead | Naga |
| Procedures Done entry | Procedure Scheduler | FO Lead against completion evidence | Naga |
| Next procedure session | Procedure Scheduler | Front Office Lead | Naga |
| Patient wait-time management | Patient Flow Coordinator | Front Office Lead | Naga |
| Daily financial closure | Billing prepares source records | Independent reconciler | Naga → Shreyas |
| Clinical readiness / medical exception | Clinical team | Appropriate doctor | Dr. Nishita |

title: 20.4 RAG Escalation Governance
body:
| **LEVEL** | **DEFINITION** | **EXAMPLES** | **OWNER** |
| GREEN | Routine issue within SOP/authority; correctable without material patient, financial or control risk. | Normal reschedule; minor queue adjustment; form corrected promptly; ordinary recall follow-up. | Role Owner / Front Office Lead |
| AMBER | Control failure, recurring miss, meaningful patient-experience issue or exception requiring management attention. | Repeated missed recalls; treatment recommendation not captured; billing correction; repeated photography miss; prolonged wait; complaint; procedure done but next-session control missed. | Naga / Clinic Manager |
| RED | Immediate safety, financial-integrity, privacy, legal, misconduct or serious reputation risk. | Patient safety concern; suspected financial manipulation; serious complaint; privacy/data breach; procedure without required clinical clearance; material unexplained payment discrepancy; serious misconduct. | Naga + relevant Founder immediately |

title: 20.5 Evidence Standard — “Show Me the Record”
body:
* Completion is proved by the approved system/register, not by WhatsApp, memory or verbal confirmation.
* If Dr. Nishita writes “Review after 6 weeks,” evidence is the booked appointment or dated recall entry.
* If a procedure is completed, evidence is Procedures Done + payment/package status + next-session status where applicable.
* If a treatment is recommended, evidence is a Suggested Treatment entry with owner and disposition.
* If photographs are required, evidence is the correctly tagged patient record.
* If an exception is approved, evidence must show requester, approver, reason, date/time and resulting action.
* If evidence does not exist, management treats the control as not completed until verified otherwise.

title: 20.6 Weekly Patient-Journey Audit
body:
Naga/Clinic Manager should randomly select a minimum of 10 patient journeys each week. Sampling should not be pre-announced or selected by the role owner.

| **AUDIT POINT** | **PASS CONDITION** |
| Appointment | Correct appointment and patient status exists. |
| Registration / records | New form or existing record/treatment forms available as applicable. |
| Payment | Required payment/package clearance occurred before service. |
| Photography | Required photographs completed and correctly uploaded. |
| Associate/Junior Doctor | Stage documented according to clinic workflow. |
| Dr. Nishita recommendation | Recommendation/prescription/investigation/review instruction documented. |
| Suggested Treatment | Recommendation captured and assigned. |
| Counselling | Disposition and follow-up visible. |
| Procedure | If performed, Procedures Done and payment/package status reconcile. |
| Next action | Consult review / next session booked or recall created. |
| Visit closure | No unexplained pending action. |

Audit scoring: Pass / Fail / Not Applicable. Any Red finding escalates immediately. Repeated Amber findings require root-cause analysis and corrective action, not only staff counselling.

title: 20.7 KPI Governance
body:
* First 30 days: establish a reliable baseline before using aggressive performance targets.
* KPIs must be calculated from source records wherever possible; staff should not self-report numbers that can be independently derived.
* Weekly review focuses on trend, exceptions and root cause — not only the headline percentage.
* Repeated KPI failure must distinguish capacity problem, training problem, process-design problem, system problem and individual performance problem.
* No KPI should encourage unsafe rushing, inappropriate treatment conversion or poor patient communication.

title: 20.8 Incident & CAPA Governance
body:
| **INCIDENT → CONTAIN → INVESTIGATE → ROOT CAUSE → CORRECTIVE ACTION → OWNER → DEADLINE → EVIDENCE → CLOSE → UPDATE SOP/TRAINING/SYSTEM** |

| **FIELD** | **REQUIRED** |
| Incident | What happened, when, patient/process affected and immediate impact. |
| Severity | Green / Amber / Red. |
| Immediate containment | What was done to stop further harm/leakage. |
| Root cause | Why the control failed; use 5 Whys for meaningful/repeated incidents. |
| Corrective action | Specific change to process, system, training, staffing or control. |
| Owner & deadline | One accountable person and a date. |
| Closure evidence | Proof the corrective action was implemented. |
| Prevention check | Whether SOP, checklist, training or system configuration must change. |

title: 20.9 Document & Version Control
body:
| **DOCUMENT FIELD** | **STANDARD** |
| Document name | Clear process/manual name. |
| Version | v1.0, v1.1, v2.0 etc. |
| Effective date | Date team is expected to follow the version. |
| Process owner | Named role accountable for maintenance. |
| Approved by | Relevant management/clinical approver. |
| Last review / next review | 30-day first review, then quarterly unless incident triggers earlier review. |
| Change history | What changed, why, who approved and effective date. |
| Master copy | One controlled master location; obsolete versions archived and not used operationally. |

title: 20.10 Training & Competency Governance
body:
| **READ → TRAINED → OBSERVED → COMPETENCY SIGNED OFF → INDEPENDENT → PERIODIC REASSESSMENT** |

* Every employee receives the relevant role charter, SOPs, authority limits, KPIs and escalation rules.
* Employee signs acknowledgement of receipt and understanding.
* Critical tasks require observed competency sign-off before independent execution.
* Backup staff are trained and signed off for the minimum cross-coverage tasks defined in this manual.
* An incident, repeated error or major SOP revision can trigger retraining/reassessment.

title: 20.11 Front Office Lead Daily Certification
body:
| **CONTROL QUESTION** | **YES / NO / EXCEPTION** |
| All arriving patients had an accountable status and owner? |  |
| All required payments financially cleared or authorised exception documented? |  |
| All recommendations captured in Suggested Treatment? |  |
| All new recommendations have counsellor/status/next action? |  |
| All completed procedures entered into Procedures Done? |  |
| All doctor-advised reviews booked or recalled? |  |
| All multi-session procedures booked/recalled/completed? |  |
| All required photography uploaded or exception recorded? |  |
| All pending investigations have a status and owner? |  |
| All complaints/wait-time exceptions have an owner? |  |
| No uncontacted/unassigned patient message or enquiry remains unexplained? |  |
| No patient remains on live board without valid status? |  |

title: 20.12 Monthly Management Certification
body:
The monthly meeting should answer five governance questions:

* Which controls failed this month?
* Which failures repeated, and why?
* What patient, revenue, reputation or operational impact resulted?
* What system/SOP/training/staffing change was implemented?
* Which corrective actions remain overdue and who owns them?

The objective is not to identify more people to blame. The objective is to ensure repeated failure results in a stronger control, while genuine individual performance or misconduct issues are handled through the appropriate HR/disciplinary process.

title: 21. Governance Implementation — First 30 Days
body:
| **PERIOD** | **ACTION** |
| Days 1–3 | Approve governance hierarchy, name Front Office Lead, independent financial checker and escalation owners. |
| Days 4–7 | Start daily huddle, live patient-flow board, end-of-day certification and RAG exception classification. |
| Week 2 | Start KPI baseline and Maker–Checker evidence checks. Naga conducts first 10-patient random audit. |
| Week 3 | Review first incidents/control failures; implement CAPA tracker and competency gaps. |
| Week 4 | First formal Front Office Governance Review with Naga + Shreyas + Dr. Nishita for clinical items; approve v1.1 process changes. |
| After 30 days | Move to weekly governance + monthly management review; review document quarterly or earlier after a material incident. |

body:
